title: Quantum Affine Type A and Level-One Fock Space

items.title: The cyclic affine type A Cartan datum and its residues
items.statement: Fix e>=2. The cyclic affine type A_{e-1}^{(1)} Cartan datum has index set I=Z/eZ={0,1,...,e-1}, root lattice Q=oplus_{i in I} Z alpha_i, weight lattice P with coroots h_i and fundamental weights Lambda_i dual to them, <h_j,Lambda_i>=delta_ij, and <h_i,alpha_j>=a_ij where the generalized Cartan matrix is a_ii=2 and a_ij=-1 when j=i+1 or j=i-1 mod e for e>=3, while for e=2 the single double-edge value is a_01=a_10=-2. All (alpha_i,alpha_i)=2, so q_i=q and the symmetrizer is d_i=1, and the pairing is symmetric. The null root delta=sum_i alpha_i and the canonical central element c=sum_i h_i satisfy <c,alpha_i>=0, <h_i,delta>=0, <c,delta>=0 and <h_i,delta>=0; the level of lambda in P is <c,lambda>. The level-one weights are those of level 1 and Lambda_0 is the basic fundamental weight. Put P^0={lambda in P : <c,lambda>=0} and P_cl=P/Z delta with cl:P->P_cl and Lambda_i^cl=cl(Lambda_i). The Dynkin diagram is the e-cycle 0-1-...-(e-1)-0 for e>=3 and the double edge 0=1 for e=2. The Cartan generator E_i,F_i,K_i is attached to alpha_i, so the node residues fixed on this page are the Dynkin indices themselves.
items.strategy: Verify the Cartan matrix axioms by direct computation ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]): for e>=3 every row has diagonal 2, two off-diagonal entries -1 and no others; for e=2 the row sums vanish with the double-edge value -2. Existence of the minimal realization with the stated lattices is [[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]] and [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]], and the fundamental weights are the dual basis of the coroots ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]], [[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]). The pairing identities for delta and c are the row-sum identities of a_ij; both are checked on the cycle and on the double edge. KMS sec. 1.1 relations (1)-(10) and KMPY sec. 5.2.1 record the same presentation, and KMPY sec. 5.2.5 shows the level-one weights and the ground state of sec. 5.2 are the ones below.

items.title: The level-one vector representation, its affinization and the energy function
items.statement: Let e>=2 and let U'_q be the subalgebra of U_q generated by the E_i,F_i,K_i^{+-1} for i in I. The level-one vector representation is V=oplus_{j in Z/eZ} Q(q)v_j with K_i v_j=q^{delta_{i,j}-delta_{i,j+1}}v_j, E_i v_j=delta_{i,j+1}v_{j-1}, F_i v_j=delta_{i,j}v_{j+1}, indices read mod e; its weights are wt(v_j) in P with <h_i,wt(v_j)>=delta_{i,j}-delta_{i,j+1}, so wt(v_j) is the image of Lambda_j-Lambda_{j-1} under the fixed section of P_cl. The crystal is B={b_j} with f~_i b_j=b_{j+1} for j=i and e~_i b_j=b_{j-1} for j=i+1; hence eps_i(b_j)=delta_{j,i+1} and phi_i(b_j)=delta_{j,i}, i.e. eps(b_j)=Lambda_{j+1}^cl and phi(b_j)=Lambda_j^cl in P_cl. The affinization is V_aff=oplus_j Q(q)[z,z^{-1}]v_j=V tensor Q(q)[z,z^{-1}], with basis z^a v_j, z of weight delta, and the U_q-action extending the U'_q-action by the degree operator d with [d,K_i]=0, [d,E_i]=delta_{i,0}E_i, [d,F_i]=-delta_{i,0}F_i and d(z^a v_j)=a z^a v_j. Written u_m=z^a v_j for m=j-ae, B_aff={u_m} carries the total order u_{m1}>u_{m2} iff m1>m2. The energy function H:B_aff x B_aff->Z is H(z^a b_i tensor z^{a'}b_j)=[i>j]+a'-a for i,j in {0,...,e-1}; it is the unique Z-valued function with H(zb1 tensor b2)=H(b1 tensor b2)-1, H(b1 tensor zb2)=H(b1 tensor b2)+1, constant on connected components of B_aff tensor B_aff, and normalized by H(b tensor b)=0 at extremal b, and H(b1 tensor b2)>0 exactly when b1>b2 in the order above. The level function l(z^m b_j)=me-j satisfies l(zb)=l(b)+e, l(e~_i b)=l(b)+1 and H(b1 tensor b2)<=0 implies l(b1)>=l(b2). The ground-state sequence is b°_m=z^{ceil(m/e)}b_{m mod e} (m in Z); it is the unique sequence with eps(b°_m)=phi(b°_{m+1}) in P_cl and H(b°_m tensor b°_{m+1})=1 for every m. For e=2 all assertions hold with residues mod 2: B={b_0,b_1}, f~_0b_0=b_1, f~_1b_1=b_0, H(b_1 tensor b_0)=1, H(b_0 tensor b_1)=0.
items.strategy: The module axioms are the explicit evaluation-module formulas (KMS sec. 1.1 (16)-(23); Stern sec. 4.1 (45)-(47)); the index relabeling u_m=z^av_j and the order (20) are KMS sec. 1.1. The weight of v_j is read off K_i v_j=q^{<h_i,wt(v_j)>}v_j, and eps,phi are computed from the arrows. The energy table and the axioms (E1)-(E4) are KMPY sec. 5.2.3 and sec. 3.2; (E3) holds because the crystal graph of B_aff tensor B_aff is connected along z-shifts and residue steps, and (E4) is the stated normalization. The equivalence H>0 iff b1>b2 is the direct computation m1>m2 iff [i>j]+a'-a>0. The level function verifies (L) by the two-case computation a'<a and a'=a. The ground-state formula is checked by eps(b°_m)=Lambda_{(m mod e)+1}^cl=phi(b°_{m+1}) and by the wrap/non-wrap computation of H(b°_m tensor b°_{m+1})=1; uniqueness follows because eps(b°_m) determines j_{m+1} and H=1 then determines the z-power. The e=2 case is the same computation on the two-element crystal with the double edge a_01=-2.

items.title: The vector representation is a perfect crystal of level one and carries a lower global basis
items.statement: B is a perfect crystal of level 1: the weights lie in the convex hull of W Lambda_0^cl with dim V_{w Lambda_0^cl}=1 for every w, B tensor B is connected, <c,eps(b)>=<c,phi(b)>=1 for every b, B_min=B, and eps,phi:B->(P^+_cl)_1 are bijective. Moreover V carries a lower global basis {G(b)}: the A-module oplus_b Z[q,q^{-1}]G(b) is a U'_q,Z-submodule, G(b)=b mod L/qL, and E_i G(b)=[1+phi_i(b)]_i G(e~_i b), F_i G(b)=[1+eps_i(b)]_i G(f~_i b), with the correction sums absent because every i-string of V has length at most 2; equivalently the two-vector i-strings are {G(b),G(f~_i b)} with F_i G(b)=G(f~_i b) on the top and F_i G(f~_i b)=0. For V_aff put G(z^m b)=z^m G(b), and G(z^m b_j)=z^m v_j up to the normalization fixing G(b_j)=b_j mod qL. The same statements hold for e=2 with the double edge.
items.strategy: The perfect-crystal axioms are read off the explicit B of item 2: the weights are the facets of the W-orbit of Lambda_0^cl, the graph B tensor B is connected by KMPY sec. 5.2.2, and eps(b_j)=Lambda_j^cl, phi(b_j)=Lambda_{j+1}^cl give the bijection B_min=B->(P^+_cl)_1. For (G), each i-string in V is the two-dimensional U_{q_i}(sl_2)-string computed in [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]]; the divided-power string lemma gives E_i G(b)=[1+phi_i(b)]G(e~_i b) and F_i G(b)=[1+eps_i(b)]G(f~_i b) with Z[q,q^{-1}]-coefficients, and the only possible correction terms would come from strictly longer i-strings, of which there are none in the e-dimensional vector module. The normalization G(b)=b mod qL and the p-stability of oplus Z[q,q^{-1}]G(b) follow from the explicit coefficients. KMPY sec. 3.1 axioms (P1)-(P3) and (G)(i)-(iv) are the source statements; their printed (5.1.1) is exactly the displayed action.

items.title: The affine Hecke algebra and its commuting action on tensor powers of the vector representation
items.statement: Let H_N(q^2) be the finite Hecke algebra generated by T_1,...,T_{N-1} with T_i^2=(q^2-1)T_i+q^2 and the braid and commuting relations, and let H~_N(q^2) be the affine Hecke algebra generated by H_N(q^2) and invertible y_1,...,y_N with y_iy_j=y_jy_i, y_jT_i=T_iy_j for i not in {j,j+1}, and y_jT_j=T_jy_{j+1}-(q^2-1)y_{j+1}, y_{j+1}T_j=T_jy_j+(q^2-1)y_{j+1} (equivalently T_jy_jT_j=q^2y_{j+1}). On V(z_1) tensor ... tensor V(z_N) there is a right action: y_j acts by z_j^{-1}, and on a pure tensor (v_{m_1} tensor ... tensor v_{m_N})z_1^{a_1}...z_N^{a_N} the generator T_i acts by the three explicit cases m_i<m_{i+1} (coefficient -q on the transposed tensor with variables swapped, plus the (q^2-1)-correction with (z_{i+1}z^{sigma_i}-z_iz)/(z_i-z_{i+1})), m_i=m_{i+1}, and m_i>m_{i+1}. This right action commutes with the left U'_q(ŝl_e)-action obtained by iterating the coproduct of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]] as in the evaluation module of item 2. The T_i are invertible, T_i^{-1}=q^{-2}T_i+(q^{-2}-1), and T_i acts as a deformation of -sigma_i. Elements T_sigma for sigma in S_N are defined by reduced words, and A^{(N)}=sum_{sigma in S_N}T_sigma is the q-antisymmetrizer.
items.strategy: The defining relations are verified to present H~_N(q^2) (KMS sec. 1.2 (24)-(31); Stern sec. 4.3 (55)-(58); Leclerc sec. 3.3 (25)-(30)); the displayed right action satisfies them by direct computation on the three cases, the y-action by z_j^{-1} being chosen to make the relations (29)-(30) hold. Commutation with the U'_q-action is the finite quantum affine Weyl-duality statement: each T_i is an intertwiner of U'_q-modules, checked on generators using the coproduct (KMS sec. 1.2 and sec. 1.3; Leclerc Prop. 6); the T_sigma are then intertwiners by multiplicativity, and A^{(N)} as well. No infinite sums occur at finite N.

items.title: The q-antisymmetrizer splits the tensor power and its kernel is the sum of the Hecke kernels
items.statement: For every N>=1 the q-antisymmetrizer A^{(N)}=sum_{sigma in S_N}T_sigma satisfies A^{(N)}(A^{(N)}-prod_{m=1}^N (1-q^{2m})/(1-q^2))=0, so V(z)^{tensor N}=Im A^{(N)} + Ker A^{(N)} is a direct sum of eigenspaces, and Ker A^{(N)} is exactly the sum of the kernels Ker(T_i+1), i=1,...,N-1. The two-term relations generating Ker(T_1+1) in V(z) tensor V(z) are u_l tensor u_m+u_m tensor u_l=0 when l=m mod e, and u_l tensor u_m+q u_m tensor u_l+u_{m-i} tensor u_{l+i}+q u_{l+i} tensor u_{m-i}=0 when m-l=i mod e with 0<i<e; these are obtained by applying U'_q to the simple kernel element v_j tensor v_j. Consequently the quotient of V(z)^{tensor N} by sum_i Ker(T_i+1) coincides with the image of A^{(N)} and is the quotient of the tensor power by the q-wedge relations in adjacent factors.
items.strategy: The factorization A^{(N)}=(sum_{sigma' in S_N/{id,sigma_i}}T_{sigma'})(T_i+1) and the relation T_i^2=(q^2-1)T_i+q^2 give A^{(N)}(T_i-q^2)=0, hence A^{(N)} acts on Im A^{(N)} by the scalar prod_{m=1}^N (1-q^{2m})/(1-q^2), which is nonzero for q not a root of unity; this proves the splitting (KMS Prop. 1.1). The inclusion sum_i Ker(T_i+1) subset Ker A^{(N)} is immediate from the factorization; the reverse inclusion uses the congruence omega A^{(N)} = scalar omega mod sum_i Ker(T_i+1) proved by the same two-vector computation (KMS Prop. 1.2). The generating relations are computed by acting with U'_q on v_j tensor v_j, using the coproduct and the evaluation-module formulas (KMS sec. 1.3 relations (41)-(42); Stern sec. 4.3 (58) for the Hecke action).

items.title: The finite q-wedge space and the normal-ordering relations
items.statement: For N>=1 the N-fold q-wedge space is wedge^N V(z):=V(z)^{tensor N}/Ker A^{(N)} = V(z)^{tensor N}/sum_{i=1}^{N-1}Ker(T_i+1), with image of u_{m_1} tensor ... tensor u_{m_N} written u_{m_1} wedge ... wedge u_{m_N}. The space is graded by weight and by total degree, and it is a U'_q-module because each Ker(T_i+1) is U'_q-stable. A sequence (m_1,...,m_N) is normally ordered when m_1>m_2>...>m_N in the order of item 2, equivalently when every consecutive pair has positive energy H(u_{m_j} tensor u_{m_{j+1}})>0; the corresponding wedges are the normally ordered wedges. The normal ordering (straightening) relations are: u_l wedge u_m=-u_m wedge u_l when l=m mod e, and for m-l=i mod e with 0<i<e, u_l wedge u_m = -q u_m wedge u_l + (q^2-1)(sum over normally ordered terms u_{m-i-ke} wedge u_{l+i+ke}, with the first term k=0 and the sum continued as long as the wedge is normally ordered). Equivalently these are the type-A specializations of the explicit kernel relations obtained by acting with U_q on v_0 tensor v_0, and they identify wedge^N V(z) with the quotient by the normalized R-1 kernel of the type-A braiding operator, R being the normalized q-transposition whose Hecke kernel is Ker(T_i+1). The A-lattice wedge^N V(z)_A is the image of L^{tensor N}, L=oplus_{a,j}Z[q,q^{-1}]z^av_j.
items.strategy: Define the quotient by the U'_q-stable kernel using the previous lemma, and verify that the displayed straightening relations lie in Ker(T_1+1) and generate it: the l=m case is (v_j tensor v_j)(T_1+1)=0 after the z-shift, and the second relation is the U'_q-orbit computation (KMS sec. 1.3 relations (41)-(45); Leclerc sec. 3.5 Prop. 8 gives the same straightening rules in the equivalent U^{tensor r} model). The identification with the R-1 kernel of KMPY is the next item: KMPY sec. 3.3 defines the wedge by N=Ker(R~-psi(z tensor 1,1 tensor z)), and Prop. 5.2.1 lists the explicit elements C_{i,j} in N whose leading parts are exactly the two relations above. The A-lattice statement is the observation that T_i preserves L^{tensor N} and that the q-wedge relations have Z[q,q^{-1}]-coefficients.

items.title: The q-wedge relations coincide with the type-A energy braiding kernel
items.statement: Under the identification u_m=z^a v_j (m=j-ae) the two-term q-wedge relations of item 6 are, up to the normalization of the basis, the explicit elements C_{i,j} of the type-A energy braiding kernel N=U_q(ŝl_e)[z tensor z, z^{-1} tensor z^{-1}, z tensor 1+1 tensor z](v_0 tensor v_0): C_{i,i}=v_i tensor v_i for every i, and C_{i,j}=v_i tensor z^{-H(i,j)}v_j+q z^{-H(i,j)}v_j tensor v_i for i≠j, with the z-shifted multiples filling the remaining terms of the second relation. Consequently the quotient by Ker(T_1+1) is the type-A specialization of the wedge V_aff tensor V_aff/N of KMPY, the normal order m_1>m_2 is the energy condition H>0, and the two descriptions have the same normally ordered wedge basis. The normalized braiding R and its denominator psi satisfy R(u tensor u)=u tensor u at extremal u, R commutes with z tensor 1 and 1 tensor z, and R(b_1 tensor b_2) is congruent to z^H b_1 tensor z^{-H}b_2 modulo qL_aff tensor L_aff for b_1,b_2 in B_aff.
items.strategy: Compare the two explicit lists: the l=m relation of item 6 is the diagonal C_{i,i} together with the symmetric z-shifts generated by z tensor 1+1 tensor z, and the l≠m relation is C_{i,j} together with its first shifted multiple, the higher multiples being exactly the remaining normally ordered terms of (45) (KMS sec. 1.3 (41)-(42) versus KMPY sec. 5.2.4 Prop. 5.2.1). Because both ideals are generated by the same explicit U'_q-orbits, the quotients and their normal-order bases coincide. The properties of R listed are KMPY sec. 3.2 (3.2.1)-(3.2.4) and (D); in the Hecke normalization R is the q-transposition T_1 renormalized so that its 1-eigenspace is Ker(T_1+1), and the congruence (3.2.4) is the energy rule of item 2 together with the q-integrality of the Hecke action. The Yang-Baxter equation needed for the compatibility of the relations is the braid relation of item 4 in H_3(q^2).

items.title: Normally ordered q-wedges form a basis for every finite wedge length
items.statement: For every N>=1 the normally ordered wedges u_{m_1} wedge ... wedge u_{m_N} with m_1>...>m_N form a Q(q)-basis of wedge^N V(z). Moreover L(wedge^N V(z)):=image of L^{tensor N} is a free Z[q,q^{-1}]-module with the normally ordered wedges as a basis, and (L(wedge^N V(z)), B(wedge^N V(z))) with B the set of normally ordered residue sequences is a crystal base of wedge^N V(z); the image of the normally ordered wedges in L/qL is a basis, and the straightening of any wedge is triangular: the reduction modulo q of a non-normally-ordered wedge expresses it in terms of normally ordered wedges with strictly smaller leading index, so the residues of the normally ordered wedges are independent mod q. Every step terminates in finitely many straightening moves, and the procedure is of length at most the number of inversions of the index sequence.
items.strategy: Spanning is the terminating straightening using the relations of item 6 (KMS sec. 1.3 (43)-(45); Leclerc Prop. 8); the termination measure is the inversion number and the induction of KMPY Prop. 3.3.9 applies verbatim. Independence: by the splitting lemma, wedge^N V(z) is isomorphic to Im A^{(N)} inside V(z)^{tensor N}; the vectors (u_{m_1} tensor ... tensor u_{m_N})A^{(N)} with m_1>...>m_N are linearly independent, which is seen by specializing q to 1, where they become the ordinary antisymmetrizations of distinct strictly decreasing sequences (KMS Prop. 1.3; Leclerc Prop. 9 uses the same specialization after a q-antisymmetrizer argument). The A-freeness follows because the ordered wedges span the image of L^{tensor N} by the integral straightening coefficients and are Q(q)-independent. The crystal-base and mod q triangularity statements are KMPY Cor. 3.3.13, Prop. 3.3.14 and Lemma 3.3.1-3.3.2, whose input (3.3.1) is the energy braiding congruence of item 7; the same triangularity is visible in Leclerc Prop. 11 (unitriangular bar-expansion with Z[q,q^{-1}] coefficients).

items.title: The semi-infinite q-wedge Fock space and its q-adic topology
items.statement: Fix a charge m in Z and let U(m) be the span of pure tensors in V(z)^{tensor infinity} that coincide with u_m tensor u_{m-1} tensor u_{m-2} tensor ... after finitely many factors. The Fock space is F(m):=U(m)/sum_{i>=1}Ker(T_i+1), equivalently the quotient by the q-wedge relations in adjacent factors. The vacuum is |m>=u_m wedge u_{m-1} wedge u_{m-2} wedge ..., and every element has the form v wedge |m-N> for N large and v in wedge^N V(z). By item 8 the vectors u_{m_1} wedge u_{m_2} wedge ... with m_1>m_2>... and m_k=m-k+1 for k large form a basis of F(m) over Q(q); the normally ordered wedges are exactly the semi-infinite wedges whose tail is the vacuum. The A-lattice L(F(m)) is the span of the normally ordered wedges, a free A-module, and F(m) carries the q-adic topology whose fundamental neighborhoods of 0 are the q^n L(F(m)), n>0; the associated completion of each finite-dimensional weight space is Q((q)) tensor_{Q(q)} F(m)_mu. The subspace F^Z(m) generated by the normally ordered wedges is a Z[q,q^{-1}]-module, and the vacuum |m> has weight Lambda_m defined by Lambda_m=Lambda_{m-e}+delta and cl(Lambda_m)=Lambda^cl_{(m mod e)}.
items.strategy: The definition follows KMS sec. 1.4 (47)-(50) and KMPY sec. 4.1-4.2. The basis statement is the N->infinity form of item 8 together with KMPY Theorem 4.2.1 and Prop. 4.2.6: any vector is v wedge |m-N>, and a normally ordered v either stays normally ordered against the vacuum or is killed by the vanishing estimates of the next item. The q-adic topology and the completion are KMPY sec. 4.3; the weight of |m> is KMS sec. 1.4 (Lambda_m=Lambda_{m-1}+wt u_m) and KMPY sec. 4.1.

items.title: Tail estimates: q-adic vanishing against the vacuum and finiteness of the weight strings
items.statement: In F(m) the following estimates hold. (i) If H(b tensor b°_m)<=0 for b in B_aff, then G(b) wedge |m>=0 in F(m); more generally for every n there is m_1>=m with G(b) wedge v°_m wedge ... wedge v°_{m_1} in q^n L(wedge^{m_1-m+2}V(z)). Dually, if H(b°_m tensor b)<=0, then for every n there is m_1<=m with v°_{m_1} wedge ... wedge v°_m wedge G(b) in q^n L(wedge^{m-m_1+2}V(z)). (ii) For every weight mu in P one has dim F(m)_mu<infty, and mu+n alpha_i is a weight of F(m) for only finitely many n; the weight multiplicities of F(m) are the multiplicities of V(Lambda_m) tempered by the Heisenberg factor. (iii) For any endomorphism C of V_aff of nonzero weight commuting with z, the vectors v°_m wedge ... wedge v°_{k-1} wedge C v°_k wedge |k+1> converge q-adically to 0 as k tends to infinity. (iv) The endomorphisms id-C constructed from the periodicity b°_{k+N}=z^c b°_k are isomorphisms on every weight space F(m)_mu with mu≠Lambda_m.
items.strategy: All four statements are the type-A case of KMPY sec. 4.2-4.3. (i) is Prop. 4.2.3 and Prop. 4.2.4, proved by induction on n and on H(b tensor b°_m): the straightening of G(b) wedge v°_m is controlled by Lemma 3.3.8(i) (the q-congruence of the kernel elements, item 7), and only the shifted pair (z^{-c}b,z^c b°_m) can survive, which strictly increases H and restarts the induction. (ii) is Prop. 4.3.1(ii)-(iii), derived from the character formula Prop. 4.3.1(i). (iii) is Lemma 4.3.3, using the periodicity of the crystal and again (i) or the dual statement. (iv) is Lemma 4.3.5, whose proof produces k with v°_m wedge ... wedge v°_{m+kN-1} wedge psi(...)(w) in qL(F(m)) and concludes injectivity of id-C on F(m)_mu. The only inputs are the finite wedge basis, the energy braiding congruence and the ground-state properties of item 2, all of which are type-A statements available here.

items.title: The semi-infinite action on the Fock space is well defined and the Fock space is an integrable U_q(ŝl_e)-module
items.statement: The coproduct action of U_q(ŝl_e) on the infinite tensor product induces well-defined endomorphisms E_i,F_i,K_i of F(m): for v wedge |m+r> in wedge^r V(z) tensor F(m+r) one has E_i(v wedge u)=E_i v wedge u+t_i^{-1}v wedge E_i u and F_i(v wedge u)=F_i v wedge t_i u+v wedge F_i u, and the sums E_i|m>=0, F_i|m>=sum_k u_m wedge ... wedge u_{k+1} wedge u_{k+1} wedge u_{k-1} wedge ... over k<=m with k=i mod e, and K_i|m>=q^{delta_{i,(m mod e)}}|m> converge in the q-adic topology and descend to F(m). On F(m) the relations [E_i,F_j]=delta_ij(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1}), the toral relations, and the quantum Serre relations hold; in particular all i-strings of F(m) are finite, so F(m) is an integrable U_q(ŝl_e)-module, and the Serre relations follow from integrability over each U_{q}(sl_2)_i. The map wedge: wedge^r V(z) tensor F(m+r)->F(m) is U_q-linear, and F(m) is completely reducible.
items.strategy: Well-definedness and convergence are KMPY Prop. 4.3.2 and its Lemmas 4.3.3-4.3.5, using the tail estimates of item 10: E_i kills all but finitely many terms directly, and the F_i-series converges q-adically because the non-normally-ordered tail terms vanish modulo increasing powers of q. The action on |m> is KMS sec. 1.4 (51)-(53); the well-definedness on the whole F(m) then follows from the coproduct shape and the vanishing estimates. The commutator relations are KMPY Prop. 4.3.8, computed on v wedge |m+r> with the toral factors produced by the coproduct; the finiteness of strings and integrability are Prop. 4.3.1(iv)-(v) and Prop. 4.3.9. The Serre relations are then forced by integrability in each rank-one subalgebra: KMPY Appendix B, Prop. B.1 (an element killed by f_i^{n+1} for some n generates a locally finite U_{q_i}(sl_2)-module, hence e_i^{s} acts by zero; the resulting vanishing of the Serre sums is Proposition B.1). Complete reducibility is KMS sec. 2.1-2.3 together with the Heisenberg decomposition, or KMPY Prop. 4.3.1(i) for the character statement used later.

items.title: Semi-infinite wedges are indexed by partitions and the action gives the node formulas
items.statement: In charge m the normally ordered semi-infinite wedges correspond bijectively to partitions by lambda <-> u_{i_1} wedge u_{i_2} wedge ... with i_k=lambda_k-k+1+m, and for m=0 the vacuum |0> corresponds to the empty partition. Under this dictionary the generators of the theorem above act termwise as node formulas: for every partition lambda and residue i, F_i|lambda>=sum_mu q^{N^r_i(lambda,mu)}|mu>, the sum over partitions mu obtained from lambda by adding one node of residue i (residue of the node (row r,column c) is c-r mod e), and E_i|mu>=sum_lambda q^{-N^l_i(lambda,mu)}|lambda>, the sum over partitions lambda obtained from mu by removing a node of residue i. Here N^r_i(lambda,mu)=A^r_i(lambda,mu)-R^r_i(lambda,mu) with A^r (resp. R^r) the number of addable (resp. removable) i-nodes of lambda strictly to the right of the added node in the content order (content=column-row), and N^l_i is defined with strictly left; both counts include only nodes of residue i and exclude the node added. The toral part acts by K_i|lambda>=q^{N_i(lambda)}|lambda> with N_i(lambda)=I_i(lambda)-R_i(lambda) the number of addable minus removable i-nodes of lambda, and the degree operator acts by d|lambda>=|lambda| |lambda> with |lambda| the number of nodes.
items.strategy: The bijection is the standard beta-number (Maya-diagram) dictionary: i_k=lambda_k-k+1 is strictly decreasing exactly when lambda is a partition, the tail i_k=-k+1 is the vacuum, and the charge shift is the z-shift (Leclerc sec. 3.9; KMS sec. 1.4; Stern sec. 1.1 remark). The node formulas are obtained by projecting the coproduct action (35)-(36) of item 6 through this dictionary: for a wedge with entries in strictly decreasing order, F_i moves the entry k with i_k=i to i_k+1 and the q-exponent collects the signed count of i-nodes to the right (Leclerc sec. 3.10 (38)-(39); LT (3)-(4) in the opposite q-convention). The toral formula is Leclerc Exercise 16 and is proved with the next item. Complete details of the termwise translation, including the coincidence of the content order with the normal order restricted to the relevant two factors, are KMS sec. 1.3-1.4 for the wedge side and Leclerc sec. 3.9-3.10 for the partition side.

items.title: The level-one partition Fock space and node residues
items.statement: Let F=oplus_lambda Q(q)|lambda> be the Q(q)-vector space with basis the partitions lambda, graded by wt(|lambda>)=Lambda_0-sum_j m_j(lambda) alpha_j, where m_j(lambda) is the number of nodes of lambda of residue j, and by degree |lambda|. The residue of the node in row r and column c is c-r mod e, so a node is an i-node if c-r=i mod e; addable and removable nodes are the addable and removable nodes of [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]. The vacuum is the empty partition and has weight Lambda_0. The Chevalley operators act by the node formulas of the previous item, so that F_i adds a node of residue i and E_i removes one; the level is <c,wt(|lambda>)>=1 for every lambda, so F is a level-one module. A partition is e-regular when no part occurs e times, and e-restricted when no column has length e; conjugation swaps the two classes.
items.strategy: This is the partition-model definition of the level-one Fock space, obtained by transporting the semi-infinite wedge model of item 9 along the bijection of item 12; the residue and weight conventions are those of Leclerc sec. 2-3.10 (his r(gamma)=j-i mod n) and of Misra-Miwa sec. 2 (color (i+j) mod n with 0-based coordinates; for the library the content convention is fixed as c-r mod e, equivalently the negative of the Misra-Miwa color, which is the same affine Dynkin automorphism for each e). The level assertion is immediate from <c,alpha_j>=0. The addable/removable dictionary and conjugation statement are [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]] and [[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]].

items.title: The addable-minus-removable node count is the level-one Cartan pairing
items.statement: For every partition lambda and every i in I, with N_i(lambda)=I_i(lambda)-R_i(lambda) the number of addable i-nodes minus the number of removable i-nodes of lambda, one has N_i(lambda)=delta_{i,0}-sum_j a_ij m_j(lambda). Consequently sum_i N_i(lambda)=1, the toral operator K_i acts on |lambda> by q^{<h_i,wt(|lambda>)>}=q^{N_i(lambda)}, and the central element K_0K_1...K_{e-1} acts by q, so wt(|lambda>)=Lambda_0-sum_j m_j alpha_j has level 1 and the toral action is the one required for F to be a U_q-module. In particular N_i(empty)=delta_{i,0}, and adding a node of residue k changes N_i by -a_ik, hence changes wt by -alpha_k.
items.strategy: Induct on the number of nodes: the empty partition has one addable node, of residue 0, so N_i(empty)=delta_{i0}. If mu is obtained from lambda by adding a residue-k node, the addable and removable i-node counts change by the standard local rule: the new node appears as a removable i-node only if i=k, and exactly the addable/removable nodes of lambda adjacent along the rim change status; bookkeeping the corners of the skew shape mu/lambda gives N_i(mu)-N_i(lambda)=-a_ik=-(2delta_{ik}-delta_{i,k+1}-delta_{i,k-1}). This is the local form of the identity and iterates from the empty partition. Equivalent formulations are Leclerc Exercise 16 (t_i|lambda>=q^{N_i(lambda)}|lambda> with N_i the addable-minus-removable count) and the standard colored-Young-diagram weight computation of Misra-Miwa sec. 2 (wt(lambda)=Lambda_0-sum m_i alpha_i). The consequence sum_i N_i(lambda)=1 is the row-sum identity of the affine Cartan matrix together with delta_{i0}-sum_j a_ij m_j summing to 1.

items.title: The node order and the signed exponents N^l_i and N^r_i
items.statement: Fix a partition lambda and a residue i. The i-nodes of lambda are its addable and removable nodes of residue i, and they are ordered by content (equivalently, for nodes of residue i, by the integer t with content=i+te; larger content is further right). For an addable i-node gamma of lambda let A^r_i(lambda,gamma), R^r_i(lambda,gamma) be the numbers of addable, respectively removable, i-nodes of lambda with content strictly larger than that of gamma, and let A^l, R^l be the corresponding numbers with strictly smaller content; the node gamma itself is excluded, and both counts use the nodes of lambda, not of the larger partition. Put N^r_i(lambda,gamma)=A^r_i-R^r_i and N^l_i(lambda,gamma)=A^l_i-R^l_i. The above/below convention is fixed by the sign rule: higher content means to the right in the sense that the q-exponent q^{N^r} belongs to F_i and q^{-N^l} to E_i, as in the node formulas of item 12. The exponents satisfy N^r_i(lambda,gamma)+N^l_i(lambda,gamma)=N_i(lambda)-1 when gamma is an addable i-node and N_i(lambda) counts the i-nodes of lambda including gamma, both N^l_i,N^r_i are integers that change by ±1 when gamma is moved past an i-node, and the unique addable i-node minimizing N^r_i is the good node of the next items.
items.strategy: The definition fixes the convention used in the node formulas of item 12; the two checks displayed are immediate from the definitions, the first because the i-nodes of lambda other than gamma split into those left and right of gamma and N_i(lambda)-1 counts them with signs. The content order is the one used by Leclerc sec. 2-3.10 and by LT (3)-(4); the worked n=2 values of Leclerc Exercise 15 (f_0|3,1>=q^{-1}|3,2>+|3,1,1>, e_0|3,1>=q^{-2}|2,1>) are the calibration example and are checked in the B-page examples of this batch. No further choice of order remains once this convention is fixed.

items.title: The Fock space node formulas satisfy the quantum affine relations
items.statement: With the node formulas of item 12, the operators E_i,F_i,K_i on F satisfy the defining relations of U_q(ŝl_e): the toral relations K_iK_j=K_jK_i and K_iE_jK_i^{-1}=q^{a_ij}E_j, K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q^{-a_ij}F_j; the mixed relations [E_i,F_j]=delta_ij(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1}); the commuting relations E_iE_j=E_jE_i and F_iF_j=F_jF_i for a_ij=0; and the quantum Serre relations sum_{k=0}^{1-a_ij}(-1)^k [1-a_ij choose k]_q E_i^{1-a_ij-k}E_jE_i^k=0 and the F-analogue, in every case including the adjacent case a_ij=-1 and the double edge a_ij=-2 for e=2 (where the relation is the cubic E_i^3E_j-[3]_qE_i^2E_jE_i+[3]_qE_iE_jE_i^2-E_jE_i^3=0 and its F-analogue). All coefficients are Z[q,q^{-1}]-valued, so the relations hold over the integral form F^Z.
items.strategy: The toral relations are item 14 together with the local change rule N_i(mu)-N_i(lambda)=-a_ik for the node of residue k. The mixed and Serre relations are proved by transporting the relation from the integrable module F(m) of item 11 through the bijection of item 12, so they hold automatically for the transported operators; independently, they can be checked directly on the partition model. The direct check is the one required by the design: expand both sides on the standard basis and compare coefficients. For [E_i,F_j] the two sides involve only partitions differing by a single i- or j-node; the exponent bookkeeping of item 15 matches the finite set of addable and removable nodes and the sum collapses to the Kronecker term. For the higher Serre cases the sum is a signed sum over chains of node additions and removals; the terms cancel in pairs by the sign-reversing involutions of LT sec. 3 and Misra-Miwa sec. 2, and the surviving terms form the Cartan-vanishing combination. The e=2 cubic case is the cancellation of the four chains of length three on the double edge; the worked examples for e=2 and small partitions are computed on the B page of this batch.

items.title: The empty partition generates an integrable highest weight submodule of highest weight Lambda_0
items.statement: In the partition Fock space the empty partition is a highest weight vector of weight Lambda_0: E_i|empty>=0 for every i, K_i|empty>=q^{delta_{i0}}|empty>, and the submodule M=U_q(ŝl_e)|empty> is the irreducible integrable highest weight module of highest weight Lambda_0. The images F_i^{(n)}|empty> for 0<=n<=<h_i,Lambda_0>=delta_{i0} and the higher products span M, all i-strings of M are finite, and the defining map from the universal integrable highest weight module of [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]] is an isomorphism onto M. The component of the empty partition in the Fock space is exactly M.
items.strategy: E_i|empty>=0 and K_i|empty>=q^{delta_{i0}}|empty> are the node formulas at the empty partition, whose only addable node is the (1,1)-node of residue 0; hence |empty> is a highest weight vector of weight Lambda_0 (item 13), and the universal property of the integrable highest weight module supplies the map. Integrability of M is the finiteness of i-strings in F (item 11), and the map is surjective by definition of M; injectivity is the standard uniqueness of the simple integrable quotient, or equivalently the nonvanishing of the corresponding highest weight space in every degree reached by the crystal operators. The identification of the connected component is immediate from the definition of the component and is used in the crystal items below. Sources: Leclerc sec. 3.9-3.10 and Prop. 12; KMS sec. 1.4 Prop. 1.4 and sec. 2.3; Misra-Miwa sec. 4 (the submodule generated by the empty Young diagram is the basic representation).

items.title: Good and cogood nodes by residue-signature reduction
items.statement: Fix a partition lambda and a residue i. Form the word in the i-nodes of lambda ordered by increasing content (item 15): write an opening bracket for every addable i-node and a closing bracket for every removable i-node, and cancel adjacent pairs )( recursively (the standard bracket cancellation). The uncancelled opening brackets are the good (or normal) addable i-nodes, and the uncancelled closing brackets are the cogood (or conormal) removable i-nodes; the leftmost uncancelled opening bracket is the good node and the rightmost uncancelled closing bracket is the cogood node. The good node is the unique addable i-node minimizing N^r_i and the cogood node is the unique removable i-node minimizing N^l_i; moreover a partition is i-regular at the good node in the following sense: the addable i-node selected at q=0 is exactly the one whose addition keeps the e-regularity of the connected component.
items.strategy: The bracket reduction is the standard signature reduction of the node word, and the identification with the minimizers of N^r_i and N^l_i is the elementary cancellation lemma: cancelling a pair corresponds to an addable i-node immediately to the left of a removable one, and after cancellation the remaining brackets are exactly the nodes at which the cumulative addable-minus-removable count changes from nonpositive to positive, which are precisely the minima of the signed counts. Sources: Misra-Miwa sec. 3 (the signature epsilon and the crystal arrows of Prop. 3.3), Fayers sec. 2 (good and cogood positions; the n-regular counterpart of Theorem 2.1), Leclerc sec. 3.10 and 3.14 for the q-adic reading of the same rule. The definition fixes the convention used by the next two items.

items.title: The crystal of the level-one Fock space is the good-node partition graph
items.statement: The Fock space F carries a crystal basis (L(F),B(F)) with B(F) the set of partitions: the residues of the normally ordered wedges of L(F) are the partitions, each partition is a residue class, and the crystal operators are f~_i lambda = lambda plus the good i-node and e~_i lambda = lambda minus the cogood i-node, with f~_i lambda=0 when lambda has no good i-node and e~_i lambda=0 when lambda has no cogood i-node. Equivalently B(F) is the graph on partitions in which lambda -i-> mu exactly when mu is obtained from lambda by adding a good i-node, and eps_i,phi_i are computed by the signature of the i-node word; the operator E_i at q=0 selects the unique term of minimal exponent in the node formula, so no cancellation ambiguity remains. Consequently the connected component of the empty partition in B(F) consists of the e-regular partitions with the induced good-node graph.
items.strategy: The q=0 leading term of F_i|lambda>=sum_mu q^{N^r_i(lambda,mu)}|mu> is computed from item 15: the exponents N^r_i(lambda,gamma) take their minimum at a unique addable i-node, namely the good node of the signature reduction; uniqueness is the cancellation lemma of item 18, which pairs every non-minimal addable node with a removable node of smaller exponent. Hence f~_i is the good-node map, and dually e~_i is the cogood-node map. The pair (L(F),B(F)) is a crystal base: L(F) is the free A-lattice spanned by the normally ordered wedges, stable under the divided powers by the q-integral coefficients of item 16, the Fock space is integrable with finite-dimensional weight spaces (item 11), and the crystal axioms are the q=0 residue form of the relations; alternatively, Misra-Miwa Theorem 3.2 constructs (L(F),B(F)) directly for the Fock space of U_q(gl(infinity)) restricted to U_q(ŝl_e), with B(F) the Young diagrams. The identification of the arrows with the signature rule is Misra-Miwa Prop. 3.3 (and Fayers Theorem 2.1 for the partition form). The e-regular description of the empty component is Misra-Miwa Prop. 4.3 and Theorem 4.7, and Leclerc Prop. 14.

items.title: The empty component is the highest weight crystal B(Lambda_0)
items.statement: The connected component of the empty partition in the Fock crystal B(F) is isomorphic, as a crystal, to the highest weight crystal B(Lambda_0) of U_q(ŝl_e): the empty partition is the unique source, it has eps(b)=0 and phi(b)=Lambda_0^cl, the component has the good-node arrows and its weight multiplicities are the multiplicities of the integrable highest weight module of highest weight Lambda_0. The complement of this component in B(F) is nonempty and consists of the partitions outside the empty component, and F decomposes as a direct sum of highest weight components in which the component of the empty partition occurs exactly once as the basic representation.
items.strategy: The submodule M=U_q|empty> is integrable of highest weight Lambda_0 (item 17), so its crystal is a union of highest weight crystals; since |empty> is the unique highest weight vector in its own component and the component is connected, the decomposition theorem [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]] together with the existence theorem [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]] identifies the component with B(Lambda_0). The good-node description of the arrows is item 19. The e-regular form and the explicit map to the Misra-Miwa realization are Misra-Miwa Theorem 4.7 and Prop. 4.3; the weight multiplicity comparison is Leclerc sec. 3.14 and KMS Prop. 1.4, both of which identify the submodule generated by the vacuum with the basic representation.

items.title: The regular-partition label convention and the Mullineux crystal involution
items.statement: A partition is e-regular when no part occurs e times, equivalently when its conjugate is e-restricted (no column of length e); the empty component of the level-one Fock crystal is labelled by the e-regular partitions, and the labels of the basic representation are taken in this convention. Conjugation lambda->lambda' ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]) maps a node of residue i to a node of residue -i and therefore interchanges e-regular and e-restricted labels; composing conjugation with the residue negation i->-i on the crystal gives the Mullineux sign involution of the basic crystal, an involution M with wt(M(lambda))=-w_0 wt(lambda) in the sense of the affine Weyl action and with f~_i M(lambda)=M(f~_{-i} lambda). The dominance order on partitions ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]) is the partial order used for the triangularity of the global basis in the next item: lambda dominance-precedes mu means mu/lambda is a horizontal strip in the convention of the Fock space component.
items.strategy: The e-regular/e-restricted equivalence is the standard conjugation statement ([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]], [[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]); the residue of a node changes sign under conjugation because content becomes its negative, so the conjugate crystal is the crystal with i and -i interchanged. Misra-Miwa Theorem 4.7 and sec. 4 give the e-regular labelling of the basic crystal; Leclerc sec. 3.14 records the same e-regular description (citing Misra-Miwa) and the sign/transpose symmetry LT Theorem 3.3(iv) (a_{lambda mu}(q)=a_{mu' lambda'}(q)). The involution is defined here as the composition of conjugation with residue negation; no identification of the Mullineux map with a specific combinatorial algorithm beyond this symmetry is asserted.

items.title: The basic representation global basis is unitriangular in the partition basis
items.statement: The semi-infinite wedge bar involution restricts to the empty component M=U_q|empty> and coincides there with the Kashiwara-Lusztig bar involution; the induced global basis {G(lambda)} of M is characterized by bar-invariance and G(lambda)=|lambda> mod qL, and coincides with the lower global basis of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] for M. Its expansion in the partition basis is unitriangular: G(mu)=sum_lambda d_{lambda mu}(q)|lambda> with d_{lambda mu} in Z[q,q^{-1}], d_{mu mu}=1, d_{lambda mu}=0 unless lambda dominance-precedes mu and lambda,mu have the same e-core, and d_{lambda mu}(q)=d_{mu' lambda'}(q) under conjugation. The elements {G(lambda) : lambda e-regular} are exactly the global basis of the basic representation B(Lambda_0), while the remaining G(lambda) extend it to the ambient Fock space; the ambient expansion is not compatible with the decomposition of F into irreducible components.
items.strategy: The bar involution exists on the semi-infinite wedge space by the q-integral straightening of item 6 and is defined on the Fock space by item 9-10: it is the semilinear map q->q^{-1} extending pr(u)bar=pr(ubar) on q-wedges, and its restriction to the empty component is identified with the Kashiwara-Lusztig bar by the characterization Leclerc sec. 3.12 Prop. 13 (the bar commutes with the lowering operators F_i and the Heisenberg generators, and is determined by these plus bar(|empty>)=|empty>). Given bar-invariance and the mod q congruence, the unitriangular expansion is proved by the same inductive straightening as the wedge basis theorem (item 8), and the coefficients have Z[q,q^{-1}] entries with the dominance and core restrictions by Leclerc Prop. 11 and LT Theorems 3.2-3.3 and Theorem 4.1. The lower global basis of the highest weight module is uniquely characterized by bar-invariance plus congruence mod q ([[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]), so the restriction coincides with it; the e-regular labels of the basic representation are item 20, and the identification {G(lambda): lambda e-regular} with Kashiwara's global basis is Leclerc Prop. 14 (also LT Theorem 4.1). The statement that the ambient basis is not compatible with the component decomposition is the first paragraph of LT (their G(mu) for non-regular mu do not match the simple components).

items.title: Node actions for partitions of size at most three
items.statement: Work out the node formulas of item 12 on all partitions of size at most three for e=2 and e=3. For e=2: F_0|empty>=|1>, E_0|1>=|empty>, F_1|1>=|1,1>, and F_0|2>=|2,1>+q^{-1}|1,1,1> with E_0|2,1>=q^{-2}|1,1>, matching Leclerc Exercise 15; the toral eigenvalues are N_0(empty)=1, N_1(empty)=0, N_0(1)=0, N_1(1)=1, N_0(2)=0, N_1(2)=2, and K_0K_1 acts by q on every partition. For e=3 the same computation lists, for each partition of size at most three, the addable and removable nodes with their residues, the exponents N^r_i,N^l_i and the resulting nonzero coefficients; the good node at q=0 is singled out in each case. All coefficients are computed from the residues c-r mod e of the nodes, and the example verifies that the level-one toral action and the node exponents agree.
items.strategy: Enumerate the addable and removable nodes of each partition and apply the residue rule c-r mod e; order the i-nodes by content and compute N^r_i,N^l_i as in item 15; apply the node formulas of item 12 and, where the partition has several nodes of one residue, compare the exponents to exhibit the good/cogood selection of item 18. The e=2 values are checked against Leclerc Exercise 15 and LT sec. 2; the e=3 values are the first cases of the e-regular/e-restricted dictionary of item 21. The verification also checks K_0K_1K_2=q and the level-one weight formula of item 14 on each partition.

items.title: The double-edge Serre cancellation in affine A_1 on partitions
items.statement: For e=2 the adjacency value is a_01=-2, so the quantum Serre relation is cubic: E_0^3E_1-[3]E_0^2E_1E_0+[3]E_0E_1E_0^2-E_1E_0^3=0 and similarly with E and F exchanged. The example evaluates the four compositions on the partitions |empty>, |1>, |2>, |1,1> and verifies the cancellation chain by chain: on |empty> only E_1E_0^3 survives and its coefficient is zero because there is no chain of three removable 0-nodes and one removable 1-node from the empty partition, while on |2> and |1,1> the chains pair as (E_0^3E_1, E_0^2E_1E_0) and (E_0E_1E_0^2, E_1E_0^3) with q-exponents summing to the [3]-multiples, leaving zero. The analogous F-computation on |3>, |2,1>, |1,1,1> exhibits the same cancellation with q^{-1} exponents; in particular F_0 and F_1 do not commute on the partition model although the relation is not the quadratic one.
items.strategy: Compute the node words for residues 0 and 1 on each of the listed partitions, use the exponents of item 15 to expand each of the four compositions, and cancel the paired chains as in the signed involution of LT sec. 3 (the double-edge case is KMS sec. 1.1 relations (9)-(10) and KMPY sec. 5.2.1 with a_01=-2). The surviving terms are collected and shown to vanish exactly because [3]=[2]+q+q^{-1} in the two surviving configurations. This is the e=2 case of item 16 and is the smallest nontrivial quantum Serre check on the Fock space.

items.title: The good-node crystal component of the empty partition for e=3
items.statement: For e=3 list the first three levels of the component of the empty partition in the good-node crystal graph: |empty> with residues of addable and removable nodes, then the partitions of size 1 and 2 reachable by good nodes, with the good and cogood nodes displayed for each partition and each residue 0,1,2. The resulting component is the beginning of the crystal B(Lambda_0) of U_q(ŝl_3), with weights Lambda_0, Lambda_0-alpha_i+delta-terms and the correct multiplicities; the example also exhibits a partition of size 3 outside the component, with its own good-node arrows, showing that the whole Fock crystal is strictly larger than B(Lambda_0). In particular the 3-regular partitions appearing at these levels are exactly the labels of the basic representation, and the non-3-regular partitions which appear at size 3 are not in the component.
items.strategy: Apply the good/cogood signature reduction of item 18 to the node word of each partition and compute the covering arrows; compare with the weights of the highest weight crystal B(Lambda_0) using eps(b)=0 and phi(b)=Lambda_0^cl at the empty partition and the tensor-free rank-one strings of each residue. The outside-component witness is verified by checking that its good-node chain never reaches the empty partition (equivalently, it is not 3-regular). Sources: Misra-Miwa sec. 4 (Prop. 4.3 and Theorem 4.7), Fayers sec. 2 (Theorem 2.1), Leclerc sec. 3.14.

items.title: Unitriangular global basis elements at small rank
items.statement: Compute the global basis expansions for e=2 and small degree: G(empty)=|empty>, G(1)=|1>, G(1,1)=|1,1>, G(2)=|2>+q|1,1>, G(2,1)=|2,1>+q|1,1,1> up to the normalization fixed by G(lambda)=|lambda> mod qL, and the dominance-unitriangular matrices of Leclerc Exercise 17 and LT sec. 4. The example verifies that the entries lie in Z[q,q^{-1}], that off-diagonal entries vanish unless the dominance and e-core conditions hold, and that the transpose symmetry d_{lambda mu}(q)=d_{mu' lambda'}(q) holds on the displayed range; it also identifies the e-regular labels (empty, |1>, |2>, |1,1,1> at low degree for e=2) as the global basis of the basic representation, and shows a bar-fixed vector outside the component whose expansion is not compatible with the component decomposition.
items.strategy: Compute the bar involution by the straightening recursion of item 22 on the displayed partitions, normalize so that G(lambda)=|lambda> mod qL, and record the resulting coefficients; the small-rank matrices are Leclerc Exercise 17 and LT sec. 4 (their matrices are the ones for the charge-zero component after the q<->q^{-1} renormalization, which the example states explicitly). The dominance and core restrictions are checked entry by entry, and the conjugation symmetry is the LT Theorem 3.3(iv) symmetry. The non-regular labels are exhibited as bar-fixed vectors lying outside the empty component, in agreement with the LT remark that the ambient canonical basis is not compatible with the component decomposition.

items.title: The whole partition Fock space is not the basic representation
items.statement: The partition Fock space F is strictly larger than the basic representation M=U_q|empty>: the one-dimensional space spanned by |1^e> (the column of e nodes, which is not e-regular) is not contained in M, and F decomposes as oplus_{k>=0} M(Lambda_0-k delta)^{oplus p(k)}, so the multiplicity of the basic representation in F is one and the higher components are nonzero. In particular no map identifies the whole Fock space with B(Lambda_0), the ambient global basis {G(lambda)} for non-e-regular lambda does not form the global basis of a single highest weight module, and the bar-fixed vector G(1^e) is not a global basis vector of the basic representation.
items.strategy: The column |1^e> has e nodes in one column, all of distinct residues 0,1,...,e-1, and is not e-regular; by the e-regular description of the empty component (item 20, Misra-Miwa Prop. 4.3 and Theorem 4.7) it lies outside the component of the empty partition. The decomposition of the classical Fock space into oplus_k M(Lambda_0-k delta)^{oplus p(k)} (with p the partition function) is the classical decomposition, valid also for the q-deformed Fock space, and is computed by KMS sec. 2.1-2.3 via the Heisenberg algebra: F(m) is isomorphic as U'_q x H-module to V_{Lambda_m} tensor C[H^-], whose U'_q-component is the basic representation and whose grading gives the multiplicities p(k) (Leclerc Prop. 12; LT sec. 1 equation (1)). The statement about the ambient global basis is the LT remark following Theorem 4.1 and the last sentence of item 22.
